STEP 1 - Vessel type: flat plate, square-ish white plate with a rim band and flat centre, no inner wall visible.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type: a square dinner plate is typically 20-30 cm; this one looks medium-large, around 25 cm across.
b) Reference: the grapes are about 2.2 cm. Across the plate's width, roughly 11 grapes laid end to end would span it, giving about 24 cm. Also consistent with a standard dinner plate.
Final width: about 25 cm (square, area about 625 cm²).

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Mashed potato (white mound, left side): covers roughly 30% of the plate, about 190 cm². It is a mound, so average thickness is about half its peak, around 2 cm. Volume about 380 ml x 1.0 = about 380 g. Reduce for a lower average, say about 300 g.
- Tomato-based sauce (on mash, plus on potatoes): a smear of about 40 cm² at roughly 1 cm average thickness counted as a mound, about 40 ml x 1.0 = about 40 g.
- Roasted potato cubes (right upper): about 20% of plate, about 125 cm², pile of chunky pieces about 2.5 cm average, roughly 310 ml x 0.8 ≈ 250 g. Potatoes are a chunky, roasted pile with some oil, so bulk density is about 0.8 g/ml. Estimate about 200 g.
- Grapes (red, right edge): count visible about 12, plus about 6 hidden underneath, so about 18 x 5 g = 90 g.
- Watermelon (bottom right): about 7 cubes of roughly 3 cm, about 20 g each → about 120 g. Roughly 3 x 3 x 3 cm is about 27 cm³, so each cube ~25 g; 7 cubes ≈ 150 g. Use 150 g.

Step 4: No hidden base layer beyond the mash itself. The sauce is included above.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g (as served):
- Mashed potato: about 90 kcal/100 g (made with milk/butter, say 100).
- Tomato sauce: about 40 kcal/100 g.
- Roasted potatoes: about 130 kcal/100 g (oil included).
- Grapes: about 70 kcal/100 g.
- Watermelon: about 30 kcal/100 g.

Totals: mash 300 g → 300 kcal; sauce 40 g → 16 kcal; roasted potato 200 g → 260 kcal; grapes 90 g → 63 kcal; watermelon 150 g → 45 kcal. Total about 680 kcal, about 800 g.
